Article Title: 'Potential to disturb public peace': Centre refuses RTI on 'Any Kuki Tribes' deletion proposal
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has refused to disclose details of a reported Manipur government proposal to delete the nomenclature "Any Kuki Tribes" from the state's Scheduled Tribes (ST) list, citing concerns that sharing the information could aggravate inter-community tensions in the violence-hit state, PTI reported.The Central Information Commission (CIC), while hearing an RTI appeal, upheld the ministry of tribal affairs' decision to withhold the information, saying the public interest in disclosing internal deliberations did not outweigh the potential risks to public order.The RTI application was filed by an applicant Micheal Haokip, who referred to a Manipur government letter that he claimed concerned a proposal to remove "Any Kuki Tribes" from the state's ST list and replace "Any Mizo (Lushai) Tribe" with "Mizo".Haokip had sought confirmation of whether the ministry received the proposal, along with its date of receipt and official file number. He also sought details of the action taken, whether it had been forwarded to the Registrar General of India (RGI) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) for concurrence, and copies of relevant communications and file notings.In its reply dated June 24, 2025, the ministry said it was the nodal authority for processing claims relating to the inclusion, exclusion or modification of communities in the ST list under Article 342 of the Constitution.It said proposals recommended and justified by the concerned state government or Union Territory administration could be processed further, subject to concurrence from the RGI and NCST, before being considered for legislative amendment.The ministry argued that disclosing information during the examination and consultation process could exert "undue pressure and influence" on authorities and allow vested interests to interfere with independent decision-making.It also cited instances where disclosure of information relating to the notification of a community had allegedly led to violence."Such disclosure of information will have the potential to disturb public peace, tranquillity and encourage enmity between the communities," the CPIO said.During the CIC hearing, the ministry reiterated that the matter was sensitive given the ethnic violence and prevailing law-and-order concerns in Manipur. It apprehended that premature disclosure of internal proposals, communications and deliberative records could aggravate inter-community tensions, exert pressure on authorities and potentially disturb public order.Haokip argued that the ministry's response was vague and failed to explain how basic administrative details, such as the date of receipt, file number and names of officials handling the matter, could be treated as information held in a fiduciary capacity.He also contended that the public-order concerns cited by the ministry were general and speculative.The CIC, however, said it was not persuaded that the public interest in disclosing substantive internal deliberations and communications outweighed the potential harm identified by the ministry.It also examined whether non-sensitive portions of the records could be disclosed after redaction under Section 10 of the RTI Act but rejected even the limited relief of providing redacted copies of the proposal and related action-taken notings.
Article Summary: The Centre has refused to disclose details of a reported Manipur government proposal to delete the nomenclature "Any Kuki Tribes" from the state's Scheduled Tribes (ST) list. The Central Information Commission (CIC) upheld the ministry of tribal affairs' decision to withhold the information.

Article Title: Not 'Amrit Kaal' but 'mehengaai ka bhuchaal': Congress criticises Centre after retail inflation reaches 2-year high
Article Text:
Jairam Ramesh targets Modi government over rising food prices, calls inflation an "earthquake" hitting household budgets

Jairam Ramesh's post on X

NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday stepped up its attack on the Centre over two-year high retail inflation, describing the current economic situation as "mehengaai ka bhuchaal" (earthquake of inflation) rather than "Amrit Kaal". The opposition party alleged that households were struggling to manage their budgets as food prices and the cost of everyday necessities continued to climb."Under the Modi government, inflation is no longer just a witch—it has now become an uninvited guest, devouring every household’s budget. From the kitchen to every other daily necessity, prices have spiraled out of control. The Modi government’s misguided policies have broken the backs of ordinary people," Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said in a post on X.Referring to the latest inflation figures, he said that retail inflation had climbed to 6.09 per cent, its highest level in two years, while prices had increased across 11 of the 12 consumption categories. He also questioned the government's response to the rising cost of living.Ramesh flagged food inflation at 8.94 per cent and pointed to sharp increases in the prices of essential vegetables and other household items.Citing figures, he said onions had become 116 per cent more expensive, garlic 60 per cent and ginger 48 per cent. He added that prices of flour, cooking oil, ghee, milk, pulses and soap had also been rising."Inflation has been rising for the past 12 years, and its real impact is far greater than government statistics suggest. But this year, even those figures have been rising every month. Retail inflation has reached a two-year high of 6.09%. What is surprising is that inflation has risen in 11 of the 12 consumption categories, yet the arrogant minister of propaganda has remained silent about his government’s performance," he said.The Congress leader further raised concerns over companies potentially reducing product quantities even as prices increase. He also warned that any increase in interest rates could add to the financial burden on households by making loans and everyday expenses costlier."Food inflation has reached 8.94%. Onions have become 116% more expensive, garlic 60%, and ginger 48%. Inflation is running rampant across everything, from flour, oil, ghee, milk and lentils to soap. Besides raising prices, companies are considering reducing product quantities. Now there are also fears of interest rate hikes, which would make both borrowing and living even more expensive for ordinary people.This is not an Amrit Kaal; it is an inflationary earthquake," he said.The Congress had also criticised the Centre on Thursday over the rising cost of essential commodities, alleging that mounting household expenses were putting pressure on ordinary consumers and calling for effective steps to rein in inflation.
Article Summary: Jairam Ramesh calls inflation an "earthquake" hitting household budgets. Retail inflation has reached a two-year high of 6.09%. Onions have become 116% more expensive, garlic 60%, and ginger 48%. Inflation is running rampant across everything, from flour, oil, ghee, milk and lentils.

Article Title: Manipur 2023 violence probe commission gets 7th extension, report due by May 20, 2027
Article Text:
The Centre has extended the inquiry into the May 2023 ethnic clashes, giving the panel another deadline to submit its findings

NEW DELHI: The commission set up to investigate the ethnic violence that broke out in Manipur in May 2023 received its seventh extension on Friday, with the Centre directing it to submit its report by May 20, 2027, according to a government order.The commission was initially given a deadline of November 2023 to submit its findings under a notification issued in September that year.Its terms of reference included investigating the causes and spread of the violence that broke out in Manipur on May 3, 2023, targeting members of different communities, and examining the sequence of events that led to the unrest.It was also asked to assess whether there had been any lapses or negligence on the part of officials or other individuals, and whether the administrative steps taken to prevent and contain the violence were adequate.The ethnic clashes have claimed more than 300 lives and forced thousands to flee their homes, widening the divide between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities.With the latest extension, the commission will have nearly four years to complete an inquiry that was originally expected to conclude within a few months.
Article Summary: The Centre has extended the inquiry into the May 2023 ethnic clashes, giving the panel another deadline to submit its findings. The ethnic clashes have claimed more than 300 lives and forced thousands to flee their homes. The commission will have nearly four years to complete an inquiry that was originally expected to conclude within a few months.

Article Title: Priyanka Gandhi's suggestion accepted, Kerala to launch Honey Mission in Wayanad tribal village

NEW DELHI: The Kerala government will implement its Honey Mission initiative in Sugandhagiri village in Wayanad district in the first phase, Agriculture Minister T Siddique announced on Friday, accepting a proposal made by Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during her visit to the tribal settlement.The Wayanad MP had suggested extending the state government's initiative to Sugandhagiri to create livelihood opportunities for members of tribal communities. Siddique, who was present during the interaction, accepted the proposal and assured that the programme would be introduced in the village. Residents welcomed the announcement with applause.The Honey Mission is a state government initiative aimed at generating employment in tribal areas by providing training in honey collection and processing, besides facilitating market access for locally produced honey.During her visit, Priyanka also interacted with residents and heard their concerns over land rights, delays in development projects and infrastructure requirements.The residents demanded land titles for those who already possessed documents establishing their rights over the land. They also sought measures to prevent delays in obtaining No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from the Forest Department for development projects.Another demand was to utilise land earmarked for public purposes but lying unused for new development initiatives.Priyanka arrived at Sugandhagiri Government Lower Primary School on Friday morning, where local women welcomed her with traditional tribal dances.Wayanad District Panchayat president Chandrika Krishnan, District Collector V Chelsasini, Pozhuthana panchayat president Nasser Kathiri, vice-president Sudha Anil, District Congress Committee president T J Isaac and other local leaders were present during the visit.
Article Summary: Kerala government will implement its Honey Mission initiative in Sugandhagiri village in Wayanad district in the first phase. Agriculture Minister T Siddique accepted a proposal made by Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. The Honey Mission is a state government initiative aimed at generating employment in tribal areas.

NEW DELHI: There were no talks regarding the merger of the two Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) factions during the meeting of MLAs with deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar, said maharashtra minister Dattatray Bharne on Friday."There was no party meeting or any political discussion on the merger. He once again challenged PM Modi to a face-to-face public debate, saying it would expose who was under the control of foreign powers and involved in anti-national activities."The Prime Minister is aware of this because he has my phone tapped," Rahul said in a video posted by the Congress on X.Rahul also shared another video on X later, accusing PM Modi of relying on a script and claiming that the pressure of facing him in a debate was getting to the Prime Minister."The stage is yours, the atmosphere is yours—yet you still needed a script. If anybody is interested, it's to understand why his brain only functions on lies day after day," Chandrasekhar said.The BJP had earlier rejected Rahul's demand for a debate with PM Modi. Union home minister Amit Shah had challenged the Congress leader to debate him in Parliament instead, asking Rahul to bring his allegations and arguments to the House rather than take the political debate to the streets.

Article Title: 'Hopeful they will come': India on inviting Pakistan to SCO Civilisational Forum in Delhi
Article Text:
Representative image

Unesco sites, shared heritage on agenda

India to host inaugural edition

NEW DELHI: India has invited Pakistan to the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi from November 20 to 22, with Union culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat saying he remained hopeful that Islamabad would participate."I should be hopeful that they will come," Shekhawat said at a press conference while discussing the invitations sent to participating countries. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend the inauguration of the forum on November 20, Shekhawat said.According to the minister, India sent invitations to 25 countries, including SCO member states, and 15 have confirmed their participation so far. China, Iran and Kazakhstan are among the countries that have confirmed their presence.The forum will be held at Purana Qila in Delhi and is intended to strengthen cultural understanding and people-to-people ties among SCO member states.Shekhawat said the grouping should serve as more than a geopolitical platform and also provide a space for countries to discuss their shared civilisational heritage.The minister said discussions at the forum would include multinational nominations for Unesco sites.The initiative is also expected to promote cultural cooperation and a better understanding of the region's shared heritage.The proposal for the civilisational dialogue forum was put forward by PM Modi during his visit to Tianjin for the SCO summit last year. The initiative was aimed at fostering closer people-to-people connections and cultural understanding within the grouping.India's invitation to Pakistan comes despite strained bilateral ties. Pakistan's minister for national heritage and culture, Aurangzeb Khan Khichi, was invited to the meeting.The SCO has continued to provide a platform for engagement between the two countries even in the absence of substantive bilateral talks.Pakistan's then foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto visited India in 2023 for an SCO foreign ministers' meeting, while external affairs minister S Jaishankar travelled to Pakistan in 2024 for a meeting of the grouping's heads of government. Neither visit resulted in a bilateral meeting.India's decision to host the first SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum was announced by defence minister Rajnath Singh at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, last month.Singh had invited all SCO member countries to participate in the initiative, which is intended to strengthen cultural ties and mutual understanding.He had also referred to the need for closer cooperation among member states on security, connectivity and regional opportunities, while stressing a collective approach to tackling terrorism.The forum in Delhi will be the inaugural edition of the initiative.
Article Summary: India has invited Pakistan to the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. The forum will be held at Purana Qila in Delhi from November 20 to 22. It is intended to strengthen cultural understanding and people-to-people ties among SCO member states.

Article Title: Start a cab rental firm with 5 cars: Govt proposes major rule overhaul
Article Text:
Start a cab rental firm with 5 cars: Govt proposes major rule overhaul

NEW DELHI: From next Jan, smaller entrepreneurs, local firms and start-ups would be able to get licences under “Rent a Cab” scheme, as govt has proposed reducing the minimum fleet requirement for such operators to five vehicles from 50, with at least two cabs per place of location.The requirement for branches in five tourist cities is being removed, further lowering entry barriers for smaller entrepreneurs, local rental companies and start-ups. The draft Rent-a-Cab Scheme, 2026, also explicitly extends its coverage to vehicles rented with or without drivers, which will widen consumer choice. This means a person who hires a cab from a licenced operator for personal use can either drive it themselves or avail the service of a driver provided by the operator.The proposed scheme, which will replace the 1989 framework, introduces sweeping changes to licencing, safety, insurance and operational requirements.Operators will be able to obtain a single electronic licence, valid across the state or Union territory, for a uniform fee of Rs 25,000, replacing separate main and branch licences. Approved operating locations can include airports, railway stations and bus terminals.The ministry has proposed a 60-day timeline for grant and renewal of licences, which will remain valid for five years. Applications for adding or removing vehicles or operating locations will be deemed approved if authorities do not complete the process within 30 days. Electronic Vahan registers and automatic retrieval of vehicle data are also expected to reduce paperwork.The draft introduces a nine-year age limit for vehicles and mandates valid registration, fitness and pollution certificates, payment of motor vehicle taxes and comprehensive insurance covering occupants as per the vehicle’s passenger capacity. Vehicles must also be free of specified pending challans and unpaid toll dues and should not figure in the NCRB’s police crime database.For chauffeur-driven rentals, operators must provide drivers with valid licences and police-verified antecedents. The cabs must also have location-tracking devices, first-aid kits and optional child restraint systems. Operators must maintain websites, provide round-the-clock grievance support and arrange emergency repairs and towing when needed. Website-based complaints must be resolved within 24 hours, while inquiries into complaints against drivers must be completed within seven days.
Article Summary: From next Jan, smaller entrepreneurs, local firms and start-ups would be able to get licences under ‘Rent a Cab’ scheme. Minimum fleet requirement for such operators to five vehicles from 50, with at least two cabs per place of location. requirement for branches in five tourist cities is being removed.

After surrendering in Feb 2026 and enrolling in a law college, top CPI(Maoist) leader Thippiri Thirupathi alias Deoji, 61, is ready for his next innings in democratic politics. Deoji speaks to TOI's Bharti Jain on his demand to lift the ban on CPI(Maoist) and make it a lawful, people-centric party. Excerpts:Also read - 'From armed struggle to people's politics': Ex-Maoist leader Deoji outlines new path, seeks release of jailed cadres I left studies and shifted to Dandkarenya forests in 1984. The socio-political scenario in those times was marked by exploitation of peasantry and women by feudalistic set-up, both in urban and rural settings. In 1978, there was a big uprising by the farmers of Telangana and a declaration was made to fight against oppression and agitate for people's rights. There was mass mobilisation and a people’s movement started to give voice to farmers, women and the weaker sections. Starting from Karimnagar, it soon spread across Telangana. I was then following this movement closely and subscribed to its anti-feudal sentiment; I joined the students' Radical Students Union (RSU) to actively 'support this cause. I was arrested several times and tortured by the police. Since circumstances did not allow us to carry out our struggle in the open, I had to go underground.Our commitment to CPI(Maoist)’s agenda of seizing power through armed revolution, had mentally prepared us to face all odds and hardships. As we continued working, our resolve only strengthened...so negotiating difficult terrain, exhaustion, poor living conditions felt normal to us.There were three sources. Firstly, we would snatch or loot weapons (from the security forces); secondly, we manufactured weapons on our own. Thirdly, depending on the funds available, we also purchased arms and ammunition from the domestic arms dealers and smugglers. We have never secured weapons from anti-India, foreign-based sources in lieu of furthering their agenda.CPI(Maoist) was mostly funded by the people after we explained to them the political cause behind waging an armed struggle and the need for weapons. Also, we extorted money from outsiders who worked in our area; like tendu patta contractors and bamboo harvesters. But we steered clear of contractors engaged in construction of roads or bridges as we believe they exploit our resources. That CPI(Maoist) had massive funds is propaganda. Our policy is to raise money to sustain us for the next three years. This money is spent on people’s issues, armed struggle and propaganda; extravagance is strictly avoided. The party never had funds in excess of Rs 30-40 crore at any time. These would largely be exhausted after fulfilling needs for the current year; only a little would be carried over to the second year. There were never any funds for the third year.After People's War merged with MCC in 2004 to form the CPI(Maoist), then PM Manmohan Singh had declared Naxalism as the biggest internal security challenge facing the country. Thereafter, the entire govt machinery -- the Centre, affected states, intelligence agencies, Central para-military forces etc -- drafted a national policy to eradicate Naxalism. This unified, coordinated fight against Naxalism peaked in 2025. Security operations were only a part of this multi-pronged counter-Naxal approach, which also focused on a development of connectivity push in the affected areas. Many Naxals leaders, cadres and PLGA commanders were arrested or killed; we also lost our general secretary Namballa Keshav Rao in 2025. This weakened the CPI(Maoist) both quantitatively and qualitatively. Its geographical area of influence shrunk. We no longer had the capability to resist the security forces. Our weapons were seized. In view of our dwindling numbers, leadership, weaponry and area of influence, our movement suffered a massive setback.In Dec 2023, at an all-India conference of DGPs chaired by HM Amit Shah, consensus emerged in favour of waging a decisive battle to eliminate Naxalism. Operation Kagaar was launched in Jan 2024 and continued till March 2026.In Aug 2024, our PB/CC members met in Dandakaranya, We assessed that the decline in Naxals’ influence that began in 2018 had acquired serious proportions. We decided to disband the big outfits like PLGA, operate in small teams and work amongst the people. The cadres were incapable of implementing these decisions. It became too much of a security risk for them to move out of Dandakaranya. They had to concentrate there, exposing themselves to the forces that had encircled the area. We paid a heavy price as we could not operationalise the tactical decisions of Aug 2024.In March 2025, we decided that we were open to holding peace talks with the govt. Our condition was cessation of operations against us. But the Central govt rejected peace talks. The anti-Naxal operations continued with severity and many of our top leaders, including general secretary Nambala Keshav Rao, were killed. This crushed our movement. After Sonu surrendered, which was not cleared by PB, we could not arrest the wave of surrenders.Had the coordinated and fierce operations by the Centre and 12 states against CPI(Maoist) not been run with a definite deadline, our movement would have lasted longer as the people’s issues we raise remain relevant even today — loot by corporates in tribal areas and feudal oppression.Given the circumstances we did some rethinking and concluded that the situation was no longer conducive to continuing the armed struggle. So we decided to give up violence and come overground. We have not surrendered to lead a comfortable personal life. We want to take up people’s issues through legal means. We will now engage in people’s politics to achieve an oppression and exploitation-free society.We have been demanding that the ban on CPI(Maoist) should be lifted. This way we can take up political activity in an open and legal manner. Even the ban on our frontal outfits must go as there has been no violent incident from our side over the past 8-10 months.It is also our responsibility to secure the release of Maoist cadres languishing in prisons. This is our demand before the Centre and state govts. HM Amit Shah claims the country became Naxal-free in March 2026; so it is only apt to free Naxals who are still in jails. They cannot go back to violence when freed, as they don't have weapons. We welcome the govt’s decision to review cases against Naxals and free those jailed for non-serious crimes. But a distinction must not be drawn between serious and non-serious crimes. Govt may argue that the Maoists have killed many people, including police personnel, and that law should take its course. But this was a war and war always results in losses on both sides. After war, peace must be established. 6000-7000 Maoists are in jail; a blanket govt order must be issued for their release.Our third demand is leniency for the 10 Maoists given death sentence for the Jhiram Ghati attack case. Our demand for blanket release of Maoists should cover them as well.Our fourth demand is to extend protection to surrendered Naxals in Chhattisgarh against revenge attacks.Politics does not exist in a rigid form. Unlike Vedas, Puranas etc that are divine scriptures and cannot be rewritten, politics is dynamic. Politics must adapt to the changing times, be it the evolving national and international situation or objective and subjective conditions; political documents cannot be construed as eternal truth. Leninism and Marxism may be our theory, but the political document must be rewritten to reflect changed tactics and strategy.We will need to consult the other leaders as well as cadres of CPI(Maoist) on whether or not to join electoral politics. If the assessment is that elections will not achieve our ends, we may stay away.Since Shah had asked us to work openly and legally, our obvious choice is to do so through CPI(Maoist). We will wait and watch and take a call on alternatives if this does not work out.As we engage in political activity as per law, we shall need a network of legal experts across the country to implement our political agenda efficiently. The knowledge of law will help us to comment and correctly interpret the law to defend activities that are within the legal framework. It will also help in perception management.Armed struggle cannot be carried on or stopped with an edict or order. Popular sentiment decides its fate. Objective conditions create popular sentiment…which then takes the form of a call to the masses and congregation. This is how people’s movements are made. Nobody can predict what will happen in the future. But we are reiterating that after embracing a life in the open, we will carry out our political agenda only within the boundaries of the Constitution and law.
Article Summary: Former supreme commander and General Secretary of the banned CPI (Maoist), Thippiri Tirupathi, also known as Deoji, addresses media during a meeting with party leaders, in Hyderabad. Deoji speaks to TOI's Bharti Jain on his demand to lift the ban on CPI(Maoists) and make it a lawful, people-centric party.

LUCKNOW: An Indonesian woman, who allegedly posed as a Kolkata resident using forged Indian identity documents and claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China, was caught by bureau of immigration officials at the Sonauli border in Maharajganj district after she was unable to speak Hindi properly during questioning.The woman, identified as Rohana, was intercepted on Nov 10 while attempting to cross into Nepal. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. Her claimed association with a Kolkata-based NGO facilitating visits to China has emerged as a key aspect of the case.According to an FIR registered at Sonauli police station, the woman initially identified herself as Li Kim Lien, daughter of Li Chin Sen, and claimed to be a resident of New Tangra Road in Kolkata, West Bengal.The complaint lodged by immigration officer stated that the woman arrived at the Sonauli immigration office around 7.30 pm on Nov 10 and presented an Indian voter ID card bearing the number ZJJ2157469.The document identified her as Li Kim Lien, born on June 29, 1975, with a residential address at 8, New Tangra Road, under Kolkata Municipal Corporation, Tangra, Kolkata.However, immigration officials became suspicious when she was unable to speak Hindi properly.Her responses during questioning raised doubts about her claimed Indian identity, prompting officials to examine her passport.The passport, bearing number X2398351, identified her as Rohana, an Indonesian citizen born on Oct 20, 1970. It also showed that she possessed an Indian employment visa.The FIR states that she held an E-3 employment visa bearing number VL9126916, valid from Oct 11, 2025, to Nov 9, 2026. Her passport also contained details of a multiple-entry Indian visa issued on Aug 11, 2023.During questioning, the woman reportedly told immigration officials that she was working as president of an NGO based in Kolkata. She further claimed that the organisation provided technical assistance to Buddhist monks travelling to China.The FIR neither identifies the NGO nor specifies the nature of its activities or establishes any link with Chinese govt authorities."We are still in the initial stage of investigation to claim or deny if the woman was involved in espionage or any other activity beyond the alleged immigration and identity-document offences," an immigration official source said.According to the FIR, officials found that the woman possessed an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and PAN card in the name of Li Kim Lien, while another PAN card was issued in the name of Rohana.The FIR alleges that the woman had obtained Indian identity documents by changing her name and address despite being an Indonesian citizen.Police registered the case under Sections 319(2), 336(3), 338 and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to cheating by personation, forgery and use of forged documents, along with Sections 22 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.
Article Summary: Indonesian woman held at Sonauli border with alleged forged Indian IDs. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. She claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China.

Article Title: Indians top again: 9.3L get OECD citizenships in 5 years
Article Text:
Indians top again: 9.3L get OECD citizenships in 5 years

OECD countries took nearly 87L new citizens during 2020-2024

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indians continue to top the list of people acquiring citizenship in advanced economies, with around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquiring the nationality of an OECD member country between 2020 and 2024, according to the 'International Migration Outlook - 2026' report released on Thursday by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), reports Lubna Kably.The figure marks a sharp increase of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh Indians who acquired citizenship of OECD member countries during 2015-2019. India remains the largest country of former nationality among those acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries, ahead of Syria and Mexico.India remains ahead of Syria and Mexico. whose nationals accounted for around 5.9 lakh citizenships in OECD countries each during the five-year period 2020–2024.Interestingly, while China was the sixth largest source country whose nationals acquired OECD member country citizenship, the numbers fell by nearly 12% to 3.4 lakh in 2020-24 as compared to the previous five-year period. OECD comprises 38 member countries – notably US, UK, European nations, Australia, Canada, Japan and South Korea.According to additional data shared with TOI, during 2020-2024, OECD member countries embraced nearly 87 lakh new citizens – Indians constitute around 10% of its new citizens.In the previous five-year period, nearly 65 lakh individuals acquired citizenship of an OECD member country – once again the composition of Indians was 10%.OECD also shared year-on-year India-specific data with TOI, showing that 2.3 lakh Indians acquired citizenship of OECD member countries in 2024, mainly in Canada (87,320), US (48,820) and Australia (28,969). In 2023, the overall India-figure was marginally lower at nearly 2.2 lakh, with the same three countries accounting for most of the citizenship acquisitions.The latest figures underline the growing permanence of Indian migration to advanced economies. While immigration flows measure the number of people moving to another country, citizenship acquisitions offer an indication of how many immigrants have progressed to acquiring the nationality of their destination country.Indians also continued to move to OECD member countries for work and study, although the pace of migration slowed. India remained the largest origin country of new migrants to OECD member countries in 2024. However, the number of Indian-origin migrants moving to OECD member countries fell by 19% in 2024, from 6.1 lakh in 2023 to 4.9 lakh in 2024.“Migration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16% of employment across the OECD,” Mathias Cormann, OECD secretary-general said. “With ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring.That means helping migrants move into jobs where they can contribute most, and giving immigrant entrepreneurs better access to finance, networks and business support,” he added.One in five STEM graduates across OECD member countries is foreign-born, and immigrants are over-represented among researchers and founders of innovative firms. Yet immigrants are also more likely to work in lower-productivity sectors, with their skills often underutilised, states OECD. The report finds that immigrant’s contribution to productivity depends on how effectively countries make use of their skills – many countries have expanded programmes to attract highly skilled workers. The gap between Indian and Chinese students studying in OECD member countries narrowed, with 8.3 lakh Indian students and 8.5 lakh Chinese students studying in these countries.
Article Summary: OECD countries took nearly 87L new citizens during 2020-2024. India remains the largest country of former nationality among those acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries, ahead of Syria and Mexico. India remained the largest origin country of new migrants to OECD member country in 2024.

Article Title: Uttar Pradesh elections 2027: Who will Owaisi-Azad alliance hurt most? Explained in 5 charts

NEW DELHI: Asaduddin Owaisi wanted a place in the INDIA bloc's fight against the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. Bihar rebuke and several olive branches later, he warned four months ago: "I have said this before, and I am saying it again: the Majlis does not want the BJP to form the government again in Uttar Pradesh. I am ready to join hands. I am ready to form an alliance. Today is the time to talk. Don't cry later after the elections are over. We don't want the BJP to come to power again."But the Samajwadi Party and the Congress, who are yet to formalise their own seat-sharing plan, did not pay heed to him.Owaisi on Thursday joined hands with Chandrashekhar Azad to build an alternative political platform in Uttar Pradesh. This time, along with challenging the BJP, the AIMIM chief declared: "If we have to die for the cause of people, it's a good deal for us; Akhilesh Yadav won't be CM, engaged in politics of entitlement."The newly-formed Samajik Parivartan Morcha, with Azad as its chief ministerial face for the 2027 assembly elections, is seeking to mobilise Dalits, Muslims and backward communities under a common political platform.And the proposition is significant. Muslims account for an estimated 19 per cent of UP's electorate, Dalits 21 per cent and OBCs around 41 per cent. The two communities at the heart of the new alliance, Muslims and Dalits, together constitute around 40 per cent of the electorate.But demographic arithmetic obviously does not automatically translate into votes.The Uttar Pradesh contest is already too crowded with the BJP, Samajwadi Party, BSP, Congress and even smaller caste-based parties within the NDA. Chirag Paswan's Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), too, is looking to expand its presence in UP ahead of the elections.So how will this new Owaisi-Azad alliance fit into the play?But first, let's rewind a bit.In Bihar, ahead of the 2025 assembly elections, Owaisi offered to contest just six seats as part of the RJD-led INDIA bloc. In September 2025, he had said that AIMIM's Bihar president Akhtarul Iman had written three letters, two to Lalu Prasad Yadav and one to Tejashwi Yadav, seeking an alliance."We are ready to take six seats. You don't even have to give us a ministry if you come to power. Just set up a Seemanchal development board. What more can we do?" Owaisi had said.The RJD-Congress-led Mahagathbandhan did not accommodate AIMIM despite Owaisi's offer to contest just six seats. The decision came despite AIMIM's five-seat breakthrough in the 2020 Bihar assembly elections, when it won all its seats in Seemanchal. Four of those five MLAs later defected to the RJD in 2022.But the party demonstrated that its support base had survived the defections. Contesting independently in 28 constituencies in 2025, AIMIM won five seats again, retaining all five constituencies it had won in 2020. Its performance came as a setback to the Mahagathbandhan in Seemanchal, where the NDA won 14 of the region's 24 seats, while the Congress and RJD managed five between them.Cut to one year later, Owaisi once again expressed his willingness to work with Akhilesh Yadav in Uttar Pradesh, that too repeatedly. The SP, however, dismissed his public overtures as "public posturing", arguing that electoral alliances were not negotiated through public statements.The SP's reluctance to accommodate AIMIM has now resulted in Owaisi building a separate front with Azad.In an interview with The TOI ahead of the alliance announcement, Owaisi said the two parties were already "shortlisting the seats and discussing who will contest from where". He also said the alliance would remain open to other parties and individuals.Now here's how the Owaisi-Azad alliance may make the parties feel its impact in upcoming elections:The SP, led by Akhilesh Yadav, may have the most immediate reason to worry. Its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) strategy seeks to consolidate backward classes, Dalits and minorities into a broad electoral coalition against the BJP.The Owaisi-Azad alliance is also attempting to mobilise precisely these constituencies, but outside the INDIA bloc opposition framework.The Muslim vote is the most immediate point of vulnerability for Akhilesh. Muslims account for approximately 19 per cent of UP's population and have overwhelmingly backed the SP in recent elections as the principal party challenging the BJP.The constituency-level data shows that there are 143 assembly seats where Muslims have a significant electoral presence: 70 seats where their population share is estimated at 20-30 per cent and another 73 where it exceeds 30 per cent.The concentration is particularly important in Rohilkhand and the Upper Doab. Constituencies such as Rampur Nagar, Chamrauwa, Moradabad Rural, Kundarki, Behat, Amroha, Sambhal, Suar, Moradabad Nagar and Najibabad have estimated Muslim population or voter shares ranging from around 45 per cent to over 60 per cent.This gives AIMIM a potential electoral geography.The analysis of 59 Muslim-dominated constituencies in the 2022 assembly elections offers another indication of the stakes. The SP won 34 seats against the BJP's 22, but the BJP's vote share was marginally higher at 39.3 per cent, against the SP's 39.1 per cent.Owaisi has repeatedly questioned why Muslim voters should continue supporting parties that seek their votes but do not offer them an adequate share in political representation.This new alliance with Azad may give Owaisi a stronger political argument. Instead of merely seeking a share of the Muslim vote, he can now pitch a broader Dalit-Muslim coalition, with Azad bringing a Dalit support base and the credibility of having won the Nagina Lok Sabha seat in 2024. This could help the alliance present itself as an alternative social and political formation, rather than just another party seeking to divide the opposition's Muslim vote.For Akhilesh, even a limited erosion of Muslim support could matter in closely contested constituencies.If Owaisi's immediate target is the SP's Muslim support base, Azad's political ambition could put pressure on the BSP and Mayawati.Dalits account for approximately 21 per cent of UP's electorate, but they are not a homogeneous political constituency.While Jatavs have remained the BSP's traditional support base, the BJP has steadily expanded its appeal among non-Jatav Dalit communities, including Pasis, who account for an estimated 4 per cent of the electorate. Through targeted outreach, welfare politics and the mobilisation of smaller caste groups, the BJP has drawn sections of these communities into its broader social coalition. This has further eroded the BSP's ability to command Dalit votes as a consolidated bloc.The BSP's vote share fell from 22.23 per cent in the 2017 assembly elections to 12.88 per cent in 2022. Its seat tally collapsed from 19 to just one. Azad's entry into the alliance could now open another front in this contest for Dalit support.Azad first emerged as a prominent Dalit voice through the Bhim Army, the organisation he co-founded in 2015 to fight caste discrimination and work for Dalit rights, particularly through education and grassroots mobilisation. His activism, often marked by confrontations with the authorities over caste-related violence, helped him build a following among Dalit youth in western Uttar Pradesh.His victory from Nagina in the 2024 Lok Sabha election gave him a parliamentary platform and established him as an electoral force, taking him beyond his earlier identity as a Dalit rights activist.For Mayawati, the challenge is not simply that Azad is emerging as a younger Dalit leader. It is that he is attempting to combine Dalit political assertion with Muslim representation, a combination that could appeal to voters looking for a new social justice platform.However, replacing Mayawati is no easy task. The BSP has a decades-old organisational network and a political identity built around Kanshi Ram's Bahujan movement.Azad will have to demonstrate that his appeal extends beyond Nagina and sections of the Jatav community. The bigger test will be whether he can attract non-Jatav Dalits, particularly in central and eastern UP, where the BJP has consolidated support among several smaller caste groups.For the BJP, the alliance is both good and bad news.On one hand, if Owaisi draws Muslim votes away from the SP and Azad takes away some Dalit support from the BSP and SP, the anti-BJP vote could become fragmented. This could work in the BJP's favour.The BJP won 255 seats in the 2022 assembly elections with 41.29 per cent of the vote. The SP secured 111 seats with 32.06 per cent.On the other hand, the alliance's attempt to mobilise non-Jatav Dalits and backward communities could challenge the BJP's own social coalition.The BJP's electoral strategy in UP has relied heavily on consolidating non-Yadav OBCs, who account for an estimated 33 per cent of the electorate, and non-Jatav Dalits.The BJP has successfully brought sections of these communities into its fold since 2014 through political representation, welfare outreach and alliances with smaller caste-based parties. These include Apna Dal (Sonelal), which has influence among Kurmis; the SBSP, led by Om Prakash Rajbhar, which draws support from Rajbhars; and the NISHAD Party, which represents riverine communities such as Nishads, Mallahs and Kewats. Together, these parties have helped the BJP build a broader non-Yadav OBC coalition across Uttar Pradesh, particularly in eastern UP.Azad's attempt to mobilise marginalised communities could put this support base under pressure. However, the alliance will have to demonstrate that it can translate its social justice pitch into votes across constituencies.The BJP, under CM Yogi Adityanath, also has an established organisational network and a much larger electoral footprint than either AIMIM or the Azad Samaj Party.For the ruling party, the bigger advantage could come if the new alliance weakens the SP's ability to consolidate anti-incumbency votes.The Congress could also face a challenge, although its direct electoral vulnerability seems less clear.The party has been trying to rebuild its presence in Uttar Pradesh through its alliance with the SP and the broader INDIA bloc.Its outreach to Dalits and minorities overlaps with the social constituencies that Owaisi and Azad are seeking to mobilise.The alliance could complicate Congress's attempt to expand its independent support base, particularly among Muslim voters who have increasingly backed the SP as the principal challenger to the BJP.The UP assembly contest has intensified with the entry of a new opposition front.Will Owaisi and Azad be able to translate their Dalit-Muslim political alliance into a viable electoral force in Uttar Pradesh? And can the two leaders build a support base strong enough to challenge established players and make the Samajik Parivartan Morcha a factor in the 2027 assembly elections? We will know in the coming months.
Article Summary: Owaisi declared Chandrashekhar Azad as the Samajik Parivartan Morcha's CM candidate. Azad said marginalised communities will use their votes to assert political power. Muslims account for 19 per cent of UP's electorate, Dalits 21 per cent and OBCs around 41 per cent.

Article Title: After EASA concern, Air India asks crew to remain on board till replacement arrives during Europe fuelling halts
Article Text:
How Air India tackled the issues:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India has asked its cockpit and cabin crew operating flights between India and North America that take a fuelling halt in Europe since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb, to remain on board till the relief crew takes over from them to operate the remaining lag of the flight. The reason: Refuelling takes place during these halts which requires the cockpit to be manned by pilots and/or engineers for the process and since passengers remain on board during this time, cabin crew has to be there to announce precautions like keeping seat belts off.There were some instances when the incoming crew left the aircraft immediately on arrival in Europe. This gap in standard operating procedure (SOP) was detected primarily at Vienna during “EU ramp inspection programme” carried out to do “safety assessment of foreign aircraft” (SAFA). Along with cabin condition issues, this led to European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) SAFA score of Air India rising to 2.7, indicating safety-related deficiencies.The same was conveyed to the Indian Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), which then swung into action along with AI to rectify the situation. The airline started deploying new or retrofitted aircraft on these routes which largely took care of cabin issues.For fuelling, AI asked its crew to remain on board till the replacement crew arrives.After taking these two steps, AI’s SAFA score has now gone to about 1.4, indicating that the issues that led to the earlier higher score have been largely addressed. “The DGCA did extensive monitoring and ensured AI followed the protocol to a T. Now AI is in the ‘good zone’ of Europe’s SAFA with the score falling from 2.7 earlier to about 1.4,” said people in the know. “Now crew often remains on board for about 1-1.5 hours after landing to oversee the fuelling process till relief crew arrives,” they add.AI’s improved SAFA score comes as a breather for the short-staffed DGCA that has been headed by non-aviation generalists for about two decades now, just ahead of facing an audit by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) from next week. It is also a relief for Air India as it is the only Indian carrier that flies to the US and will be examined closely by FAA for that reason. In operational terms, this should lead to less checks during fuelling stops in Europe and fewer delays on that count during halts there for AI.Refuelling: The SOP is that an engineering team and/or pilots should be in the flight deck when an aircraft is getting refuelled to coordinate with the fuelling staff. The cabin crew has to announce that passengers must not have their seat belts on when fuelling is taking place.The AI circular for pilots, reiterating the incoming set remains on board till it’s replaced by the relief crew. “Before commencing fuelling, the flight deck crew will be informed by engineering. If flight crew are unable to attend the flight deck during refueling, they shall request a qualified engineer to attend the flight deck,” says his circular.It adds: “NO PED (personal electronic devices) NO SMOKING / NO DEVICES / EXIT signs shall be illuminated as an indication to the cabin crew that fuelling is in progress. 'Seat belt' sign must be off. Known high energy equipment such as HF radios shall not be operated (during refuelling).”
Article Summary: Air India has asked its cockpit and cabin crew operating flights between India and North America to remain on board till the relief crew takes over from them. Refuelling takes place during these halts which requires the cockpit to be manned by pilots and/or engineers. The cabin crew has to announce that passengers must not have their seat belts on during fuelling.

Article Title: Ssr: Rajasthan SSR draft counts 11 lakh more voters than SIR list
Article Text:
Rajasthan's draft voter roll shows 5.26 crore electors, leaving discrepancies across three official rolls.

Changes in Raj rolls can be sought till Jan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JAIPUR: Rajasthan's latest draft electoral roll, published Thursday under the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, has produced a fresh numbers puzzle. It records about 5.26 crore voters - about 11 lakh more than the 5.15 crore in the final Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll published in Feb.But the number is still far below another official figure in circulation: State Election Commission's final electoral roll, which stood at 5.45 crore voters in early Oct.That leaves Rajasthan with three voter counts in less than a year - 5.15 crore in the final SIR roll, 5.45 crore in the SEC roll, and now 5.26 crore in the ECI-linked SSR draft. The latest figure sits between the two, but does not settle the central question: why official rolls for the same state show such wide variation. According to Chief Electoral Officer Naveen Mahajan, the SSR draft has 2,75,24,780 male voters, 2,51,42,052 female voters and 584 transgender voters. The qualifying date for the revision is Jan 1, 2027. EC has opened claims and objections from Nov 12 to Dec 11. The final roll will be published on Jan 4, 2027.The difference between SIR and SSR is critical to understanding the numbers. SIR is a deeper verification exercise in which booth-level officers conduct house-to-house enumeration.Existing voters are given pre-filled forms and are required to submit them for their names to be considered in the revised roll.SSR begins with the last published final roll. Existing voters are generally carried forward and not required to prove eligibility afresh merely to retain their names. The exercise is meant to update the roll through additions, deletions and corrections.This difference in method explains why a draft SSR roll may not mirror a final SIR roll. But the wider problem is the coexistence of sharply different official numbers. The SSR draft is around 11 lakh higher than the final SIR roll, yet around 18 lakh lower than the SEC’s early-Oct roll.The draft rolls have been shared with recognised political parties and uploaded on the CEO website. Voters can seek inclusion, deletion or correction through the prescribed forms before the final roll is frozen in January.Mahajan urged eligible citizens to verify their names in the draft roll and apply for inclusion if their names are missing. Those completing 18 years by Jan 1, 2027, can apply for enrolment. Young citizens turning 18 by Oct 1, 2027, can also submit advance applications.
Article Summary: Rajasthan's latest draft electoral roll has produced a fresh numbers puzzle. It records about 5.26 crore voters - about 11 lakh more than the 5.15 crore in the final Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll published in Feb. The number is still far below another official figure in circulation: State Election Commission's final electoral roll.

Article Title: India simplifies visa rules: Categories cut to 9 from 13, application fields reduced by up to 70%
Article Text:
The rationalisation of visitor visa, earlier called tourist visa, allows flexibility for short and long stays.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Having simplified its visa regime by cutting the total visa categories to 9 from 13 and sub-categories to 23 from 49 and also reducing the information sought from foreign applicants across all 23 sub-categories, the ministry of home affairs (MHA) will be MHA updating its IT systems by year-end, to grant visas per new rationalisation."The step aims at making it (visa regime) more compact, coherent and responsive to the requirements of foreign nationals visiting India," the home ministry said in a statement on Wednesday. As part of the revamp, the main visa categories were first cut on 22 to 13 and sub-categories to 49 from 63 in October last year, and further to 9 and 23 respectively on August 27 this year. This simplification was done after studying the visa system followed by the developed countries as well as the global standards."The consolidation of similar purposes of travel is aimed at providing greater clarity and ease in identifying the appropriate visa category while facilitating legitimate foreign arrivals," said a ministry spokesperson.Currently electronic visa or e visa is processed by electronic travel authorization under 13 sub categories. The e-visa facility is available to nationals of 172 countries.The MHA has also made visa application simpler, cutting the fields/columns by upto 70% across all 23 sub-categories of visas."The initiative aims to significantly reduce the information required from foreign nationals, while retaining essential details necessary for visa processing. This will reduce time and effort required to complete the application and also enhance administrative efficiency by facilitating more focused scrutiny and processing of visa application," said MHA.The rationalisation of visitor visa, earlier called tourist visa, allows flexibility for short and long stays. The name visitor visa reflects a broader range of permitted purposes beyond conventional tourism. The category has been organised into two sub-categories, V-1 and V-2. V-1 covers short-term activities such as business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats, and short term courses. It is granted for 30 days with multiple entries. V2 is for longer-duration visits, with validity of 1, 5 or 10 years, as specified.The medical visa framework retains separate provisions for treatment under conventional and AYUSH systems. M-1 Visa covers medical treatment other than treatment under AYUSH systems, while M-3 Visa covers treatment under AYUSH systems. M-1 and M-3 Visas, including their e-Visa variants, will be granted for one year as a default option with multiple entries.This arrangement gives patients greater predictability when treatment involves multiple consultations, follow-up appointments or staged procedures.In the student visa category, S-1 covers school and college education while the S-2 is meant for PhD and research scholars in Indian universities.Business visas shall now also divided into B-1 and B-2. B-1 Visa covers long-term, licence-based business activities, including foreign nationals seeking to establish industrial or business ventures in India. B-2 Visa covers short-term, contract-based business activities, including Production Investment Business, conferences, sports, performative arts and films.A specific provision has also been made for foreign subject-matter specialists, engineers and technical personnel engaged by Indian companies. Such personnel may be granted a production investment business visa under the B-2 category through the e-Visa platform. This was earlier granted under e-B4 visa nomenclature."This differentiation gives businesses greater clarity when planning long-term investments as against short-term contractual assignments. The dedicated provision for technical specialists can facilitate timely deployment of expertise for setting up and operationalising industrial facilities, transferring technology, etc," as per MHA.The ministry said the changes in visa regime reduce overlap between visa categories and make the framework easier to navigate for visitors, patients, students, researchers, investors and business professionals. The rationalisation is intended to support legitimate travel, education, healthcare and economic engagement with India through clearer, purpose-based visa options, subject to applicable eligibility criteria and conditions.
Article Summary: Ministry of home affairs (MHA) will be MHA updating its IT systems by year-end, to grant visas per new rationalisation. The rationalisation of visitor visa, earlier called tourist visa, allows flexibility for short and long stays. The name visitor visa reflects a broader range of permitted purposes beyond conventional tourism.

Indians continue to top the list of people acquiring citizenship in advanced economies, with around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquiring the nationality of an OECD member country between 2020 and 2024, according to the ‘International Migration Outlook – 2026’ report released on Thursday by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).The figure marks a sharp increase of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh Indians who acquired citizenship of OECD member countries during 2015–2019. India remains the largest country of former nationality among those acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries, ahead of Syria and Mexico, whose nationals accounted for around 5.9 lakh citizenships in these countries each during the five-year period 2020–2024. Interestingly, while China was the sixth largest source country whose nationals acquired OECD member country citizenship, the numbers fell by nearly 12% to 3.4 lakh in 2020-2024 as compared to the previous five-year period.OECD comprises 38 member countries – notably US, UK, European nations, Australia, Canada, Japan and South Korea.According to additional data shared with TOI, during the five-year period 2020-2024, OECD member countries embraced nearly 87 lakh new citizens – Indians constitute around 10% of its new citizens. In the previous five-year period, nearly 65 lakh individuals acquired citizenship of an OECD member country – once again the composition of Indians was 10%.OECD also shared year-on-year India-specific data with TOI, showing that 2.30 lakh Indians acquired citizenship of OECD member countries in 2024, mainly in Canada (87,320), the US (48,820) and Australia (28,969). In 2023, the overall India-figure was marginally lower at nearly 2.25 lakh, with the same three countries accounting for most of the citizenship acquisitions.The report attributes the increase in Indian citizenship in OECD member countries to the growth of Indian communities in several member countries, particularly Canada. A total of 2.61 lakh Indians became Canadian citizens during 2020–2024, an increase of 150% compared with the preceding five-year period. The numbers were also high in the US, the UK and Australia.The latest figures underline the growing permanence of Indian migration to advanced economies. While immigration flows measure the number of people moving to another country, citizenship acquisitions offer an indication of how many immigrants have progressed to acquiring the nationality of their destination country.The OECD's latest report also records a rise in new citizenships from various nationalities across its member countries. Around 3 million (30 lakh) people acquired the nationality of an OECD country in 2025. The US accounted for almost 9 lakh new citizens – a rise of 9% over 2024, followed by Germany and Spain with 3 lakh new citizens each registering a rise of 9% and 6% over the previous year. Canada ranked only fourth in 2025, due to a 22% drop, and registered nearly 3 lakh new citizens. However, India's strong showing is particularly evident in Canada, which has been a major destination for Indian migrants over the past decade, with established communities contributing to the pool of people eligible to apply for citizenship.Indians also continued to move to OECD member countries for work and study, although the pace of migration slowed. India remained the largest origin country of new migrants to OECD member countries in 2024. However, the number of Indian-origin migrants moving to OECD member countries fell by 19% in 2024, from 6.07 lakh in 2023 to 4.94 lakh in 2024.“Migration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16% of employment across the OECD,” Mathias Cormann, OECD Secretary-General said. “With ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring. That means helping migrants move into jobs where they can contribute most, and giving immigrant entrepreneurs better access to finance, networks and business support,” he added.Immigrants accounted for 12% of the OECD member countries population in 2025, up from 9% in 2015. In just over half of OECD countries, immigrants contributed at least 50% of employment growth between 2014 and 2024.One in five STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) graduates across OECD member countries is foreign-born, and immigrants are over-represented among researchers and founders of innovative firms. Yet immigrants are also more likely to work in lower-productivity firms and sectors, with their skills often underutilised, states OECD. The report finds that immigrant’s contribution to productivity depends on how effectively countries make use of their skills and support investment and innovation – many countries have expanded programmes to attract highly skilled workers.International student inflows to OECD member countries fell from 19 lakh in 2024 to 16 lakh in 2025, with the decline concentrated in traditional English-speaking destinations. In contrast, European countries continued to attract growing numbers of international students, especially Austria, Germany and Italy. China and India remained the largest source countries.The gap between Indian and Chinese students studying in OECD member countries narrowed, with 8.3 lakh Indian students and 8.50 lakh Chinese students studying in these countries.With restrictive immigration policies being introduced in several OECD member countries such as the US, UK, Canada and Australia, immigration experts believe that the number of temporary workers and students could show a decline over the next few years. However, it is likely that Indians will continue to top the charts in citizenship acquisition and their foray overseas for work and study.Permanent migration to OECD member countries declined by 1.6% in 2025, falling for the second consecutive year, but remained historically high at nearly 60 lakh new permanent immigrants. Permanent migration covers people moving for family reunification, work or humanitarian reasons with a long term right to stay. With restrictive policies in major destination countries, this has shown a decline.
Article Summary: 9.25 lakh Indians acquired citizenship in rich nations in 5 years, up 41%: OECD. The figure marks a sharp increase of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh Indians who acquired citizenship of OECD member countries during 2015–2019. India remains the largest country of former nationality among those acquiring citizenship in OECD member nations, ahead of Syria and Mexico.

NEW DELHI: The next time you pick up a milk packet, a curd carton or a paneer pack, you may notice a new symbol on the label. From July 1, 2028, all milk and milk products, including composite milk products, will have to carry a distinctive, standardised blue-and-white droplet logo, providing a uniform identification mark for the category.The logo features a white droplet against a blue square background. FSSAI officials told TOI that the mark is intended to help consumers readily identify products in this category at the point of purchase, strengthen their awareness and understanding of the regulatory identity of milk and milk products, and facilitate quicker recognition of relevant information on product labels. It is also aimed at bringing greater consistency to labelling practices.The requirement has been notified through the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026, published in the Gazette on November 9. The amendment to the 2020 labelling regulations will come into force on July 1, 2028.The authority has prescribed minimum dimensions for the logo according to the area of the package's principal display panel. The blue square must measure at least 6 mm on each side for panels up to 100 sq cm, 8 mm for panels measuring 100 to 500 sq cm, 12 mm for panels measuring 500 to 2,500 sq cm, and 16 mm for panels larger than 2,500 sq cm.The Gazette also specifies the minimum dimensions of the white droplet inside the square. For the smallest, 6 mm logo, the droplet must be at least 4.56 mm high and 3 mm wide. For the larger logo sizes, these dimensions increase to 6.08 mm by 4 mm, 9.12 mm by 6 mm and 12.16 mm by 8 mm, respectively.The amendment follows a draft proposal issued in February 2025, when FSSAI invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders. The authority said it considered the feedback received before finalising the regulations.

SRINAGAR: At the end of the marriage season, wedding chefs, called wazas in Kashmir, have created a storm in the Valley by announcing that they will stop serving wazwan, the traditional multi-course Kashmiri meal, after 10 pm in an attempt to curb increasingly late-night wedding feasts. The decision is being widely debated on social media in Kashmir and politics, it appears, has taken a backseat for the moment.The dinner deadline will take effect from the next marriage season, which begins in May, according to All Kashmir Waza Association president Ghulam Nabi Baba. Under the new proposed arrangement, Baba said lunch wazwan would be served at 2 pm and dinner at around 10 pm. He said members who fail to follow the association’s rules would be removed.Baba said the decision was taken at an association meeting at Rajouri Kadal, in Srinagar’s old city, on Wednesday in response to the growing trend of delayed groom arrivals at wedding venues. Some grooms, he said, reach the bride’s home as late as 3 or 4 am, when they should be having a feast much before 10 pm.“From next season, starting in May, this will not be tolerated,” Baba told TOI. With the changing security situation in the Valley, late-night weddings have become the norm, but the wazas are not happy about it.They have their reasons. Baba said serving wazwan past midnight creates problems as younger people are reluctant to join the profession, presuming it more demanding, while labourers hired for the day are unwilling to work through the night after remaining on duty for long hours.Baba said the timing decision would be implemented through the association, which is 60 years old and has chefs from across the Valley as members. “Our association is registered and has at least 40,000 members,” he said. “We will introduce an agreement that the groom’s or bride’s family hiring us will have to sign,” he said.In South Kashmir, Nazir Ahmad Waza said the delays were affecting the livelihoods of chefs and their ability to manage bookings. “The lack of fixed timings is affecting our business. We are unable to commit to dates due to delays. The delays are hitting everyone hard — customers and guests who come to enjoy the feast,” he said.The association’s announcement has prompted wider social media debate. “I have a request for the Waza Association. Please do not accept processed spices, cockscomb, garlic paste, colourants or powdered milk. Give us the original wazwan we once cherished and do not make more than seven dishes,” reads a post on Facebook.“Restricting the timing of wazwan functions and ensuring that they do not continue beyond reasonable hours is certainly a need of society… But there is another equally important issue: Who is monitoring the rates charged by wazas?” read another post.One social media post accusing them of experimenting with more mutton dishes and making a marriage feast a costly affair shows mutton dishes prepared in grenade and AK-47 shapes in response to Baba’s deadline statement. Baba said the association will encourage its members to follow the traditional seven-course meal.
Article Summary: All Kashmir Waza Association president Ghulam Nabi Baba said lunch wazwan would be served at 2 pm and dinner at around 10 pm. The decision was taken at an association meeting at Rajouri Kadal, in Srinagar’s old city. The dinner deadline will take effect from the next marriage season.

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has written to the Ladakh administration seeking clarification over a 60-day order restricting his movement, alleging that he has effectively been placed under house arrest without any formal direction or legal justification.In his representation, dated November 12, Wangchuk said the order issued by the office of the additional district magistrate, Leh, on November 11 under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) had curtailed his freedom of movement and speech. HYDERABAD: Surrendered CPI(Maoist) politburo member Thippiri Thirupathi alias Deoji, who was de-facto chief of the outfit after general secretary Namballa Keshav Rao was killed in May 2025, has decided to embrace democratic politics and raise people-centric issues in an open and legal manner. He has, however, ruled out entering electoral politics just yet.Currently studying law in a college in Hyderabad, Deoji wants to repurpose CPI(Maoist) into the party vehicle for carrying out his political plans. For this, he has demanded that the ban on CPI(Maoist) be lifted and even agreed on the need to rewrite the outfit’s political document to revise its tactics and strategy from “seizing power through armed struggle” to “people’s politics”.“The current circumstances are not conducive to continuing armed struggle...so we have decided to shun violence, illegal and secret activities and take up open and lawful political activity. In politics, our central agenda shall be to build an oppression and exploitation-free society...we will agitate for people’s rights and organise protests,” he stated in an exclusive interview to TOI more than 8 months after he surrendered before the Telangana police and joined the mainstream.Deoji said lifting of ban on CPI(Maoist) will give him an established platform to practice politics. However, if the ban is not reviewed anytime soon, he is open to floating an alternative political outfit. Apart from ending the UAPA ban on CPI(Maoist) and its fronts, the surrendered leader demanded that the Maoists still in jails should be freed. Though the state govts are reviewing non-serious cases against Maoists, Deoji is opposed to a distinction being drawn between serious and non-serious offences. “A blanket political call must be taken to drop cases against Maoists, irrespective of the gravity,” he said and even sought similar leniency for the 10 Maoists awarded death sentence for the Jhiram Ghati massacre.The Central govt, as per sources, has consistently opposed a “general amnesty” to Maoists. An NIA court had recently convicted and awarded death sentence to 10 Maoists in the case relating to the May 2013 Jhiram Ghati attack, which had killed 27 people including top Congress leaders in Chhattisgarh.Deoji revealed that the armed Naxal movement was severely hit due to sustained, decisive operations undertaken by the Central forces between Jan 2024 and March 2026, which literally “locked-in” the CPI(Maoist) leaders and cadres in Dandakaranya. Though the politburo and central committee leaders had, at their last meeting in August 2024, agreed to revise tactics — like disbanding the bigger formations like PLGA, operating in small teams, asking cadres to move out of Dandakaranya and focusing on working among the people — these could not be implemented as the leadership and cadres were encircled and overwhelmed by well-equipped counter-Naxal forces.“Our leaders, including general secretary Nambala Keshav Rao alias Basavaraju, were killed. Weapons were seized and cadres got concentrated in one place. This crushed our movement,” he revealed.Deoji said Mallojula Venugopal Rao alias Sonu surrendered without any go-ahead from the CPI(Maoist) leadership. “This triggered a chain reaction and we were unable to arrest the wave of surrenders,” he said.The August 2024 meeting of the apex Maoist leadership was attended by Basavaraju, former general secretary Ganpathy, politburo members Deoji and Sonu and central committee members Malla Raji Reddy alias Sangram, Kadari Satyanarayana Reddy alias Kosa, Katta Ramachandra Reddy and Ramdher.Basavaraju, Kosa and Katta Ramachandra Reddy were later killed by the counter-Naxal forces. Article Title: India makes gains against TB, deaths down 38% since 2015: Centre
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: India's estimated TB deaths declined by 38% between 2015 and 2025, while the mortality rate fell from 28 to 18 per lakh population, according to the Union health ministry. The World Health Organization 's Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 says India achieved the first 35% mortality-reduction milestone under its End TB Strategy in 2025, five years after the original 2020 deadline.The ministry also reported a 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB, attributing the progress to intensified case-finding, rapid molecular diagnostics, AI-enabled portable chest X-rays, timely treatment and nutritional support.Drug-resistant TB remains a challenge, with only 42% of the estimated 3.7 lakh global rifampicin-resistant TB cases in 2025 enrolled on treatment. India and four other high-burden countries account for around 60% of the global treatment gap.The government's intensified screening campaign has meanwhile detected nearly 15 lakh people with TB who had no apparent symptoms. Between December 7, 2024, and November 8, 2026, the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan covered more than 25 crore people, with over 11 crore chest X-rays and 3 crore molecular tests conducted.The campaign detected 48.64 lakh TB cases, including 14.97 lakh asymptomatic cases, according to ministry data released on Thursday.The first intensified 100-day campaign was launched in December 2024 in 347 high-priority districts across 33 states and Union Territories before being expanded nationwide. A second 100-day campaign began on March 24 this year, targeting 1.58 lakh high-risk villages and wards, congregate settings and vulnerable populations.The detection of asymptomatic cases is significant because people without recognisable symptoms may not approach health facilities for testing. Active screening can help identify them and connect them to treatment earlier.The ministry attributed the improvement in mortality and treatment outcomes to intensified case-finding, rapid molecular diagnostics, AI-enabled portable chest X-rays, timely treatment and nutritional support. The Ni-kshay digital platform supports patient tracking and treatment monitoring, while the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana provides nutritional assistance to eligible patients. The Ni-kshay Mitra initiative mobilises individuals and organisations to support people undergoing treatment.The ministry said 67,933 panchayats were declared TB-free in 2025 and that 96% of the TB programme's funding requirements were met through domestic resources.However, the WHO report flags an important data gap. India's TB incidence estimates for 2010-2025 are under review following the completion of the first round of district-level sentinel surveillance and a national TB prevalence survey. WHO is expected to update India's country profile after technical discussions on the new data, likely in early 2027.India accounts for about a quarter of the estimated global TB burden. Globally, 10.6 million people developed TB in 2025 and 1.13 million died of the disease. The global decline in TB incidence between 2015 and 2025 was only 14%, far short of the End TB Strategy's 50% reduction milestone for 2025.
Article Summary: India's estimated TB deaths declined by 38% between 2015 and 2025, while the mortality rate fell from 28 to 18 per lakh population. The World Health Organization's Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 says India achieved the first 35% mortality-reduction milestone under its End TB Strategy.
